Belarusian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Proto-Slavic *krajь.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [kraj]
  • Audio:(file)

Noun

[edit]

край • (kraj) m inan (genitive кра́ю, nominative plural краі́, genitive plural краёў)

  1. end
  2. region
  3. country, land

Bulgarian

[edit]
Bulgarian Wikipedia has an article on:
край
Wikipedia bg

Etymology

[edit]

From Proto-Slavic *krajь.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [kraj]
  • Audio (Standard Bulgarian):(file)
  • Rhymes: -aj

Noun

[edit]

край • (kraj) m

  1. end, finish
  2. termination, completion, conclusion, close, ending
    Synonym: завъ́ршек (zavǎ́ršek)
  3. edge, brink, verge, brim
  4. outskirt, edge, skirt, fringe, end
    Synonym: покра́йнина (pokrájnina)
  5. vicinity, region, parts
    Synonym: о́бласт (óblast)
  6. corner, recess
    Synonym: кът (kǎt)

[edit]

krája

1Rare.

Preposition

[edit]

край • (kraj)

  2. by; along
    • 1994, “Там, край реката [There, by the river]”, performed by Тоника (Tonika):
      Де ми каза две слова – там, край реката.
      De mi kaza dve slova – tam, kraj rekata.
      Where you told me a couple of words – there, by the river.

[edit]
  • край- (kraj-)

Pannonian Rusyn

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old Slovak kraj, from Proto-Slavic *krajь.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈkraj]
  • Rhymes: -aj
  • Hyphenation: край

Noun

[edit]

край (kraj) m inan (diminutive країчок, relational adjective крайнї or крайови)

  1. end, ending, finish
    на краю лєса ― na kraju ljesa ― at an end of the forest
  2. region, area
    у хторим краю варошу биваце? ― u xtorim kraju varošu bivace? ― which region of town do you live in?
  3. country, province, landscape, scenery
    Synonyms: обласц (oblasc), предїл (predjil)
  4. homeland, home
    Synonyms: (Serbism) завичай (zavičaj), отечество (otečestvo), оцовщина (ocovščina), родни край (rodni kraj)
    по велїх рокох врацел ше зоз швета до краю ― po veljix rokox vracel še zoz šveta do kraju ― after many years he returned from the outside world to his homeland
  5. shore, coast
    привеслал ґу краю ― priveslal gu kraju ― he rowed to the shore
    чамец плїва коло краю ― čamec pljiva kolo kraju ― the boat floated along the shore
  6. arm (of scales, crane, etc.), extremity
  7. rim, edge, periphery
    Synonym: орубенєц (orubenjec)

Russian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *krajь.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [kraj]
  • Audio:(file)
  • Audio (Saint Petersburg):(file)
  • Rhymes: -aj

Noun

[edit]

край • (kraj) m inan (genitive кра́я, nominative plural края́, genitive plural краёв, relational adjective краево́й, diminutive кра́ешек)

  1. border, edge, brink, brim, fringe
  2. side, rim
  3. land, country
  4. krai, territory (in Russia)

△ Irregular.

2 на краю́ (na krajú) is used in the sense "on the edge/boundary/side"; в краю́ (v krajú) is used in the sense "in the land/country". в кра́е (v kráje) is used in the sense "in the krai/administrative region".

  • страна́ (straná), о́бласть (óblastʹ), ме́стность (méstnostʹ)

  • кра́йний (krájnij), бескра́йний (beskrájnij), бескра́йный (beskrájnyj)
